entries.title: Centered second and fourth moments under a diameter bound
entries.statement: If a real random variable X has mean zero and support in an interval of length D, with a=E X^2 and b=E X^4, then a<=D^2/4 and b+3a^2<=D^2 a.
entries.proof_text: For support [l,h], E[(X-l)(h-X)]>=0 gives a<=-lh<=(h-l)^2/4. For an independent copy X-prime, (X-X-prime)^4<=D^2(X-X-prime)^2 pointwise. Centering gives E(X-X-prime)^4=2b+6a^2 and E(X-X-prime)^2=2a; divide by 2.
assumptions: X is supported in an interval of finite length D

entries.title: Strict lower bound for a separating Cauchy-profile minimum
entries.statement: Let mu be a probability law with compact support of diameter at most D>0 and let R>0. Every local minimum of F(u)=integral ((x-u)^2+R^2)^(-1)dmu(x) has F(u)>1/D^2.
entries.proof_text: At a stationary point set y=R^2, Z=integral ((x-u)^2+y)^(-2)dmu, and reweight dQ=Z^(-1)((x-u)^2+y)^(-2)dmu. Under Q, X=x-u is centered; let a=E X^2,b=E X^4. Normalization gives 1/F=(b+2ay+y^2)/(a+y). Differentiation gives F-second/(2Z)=3-4y E_Q[1/(X^2+y)]. If F-second>=0, Jensen gives y<=3a. The moment bounds then imply 1/F-D^2<=((y-3a)(y+a)+(4a-D^2)y)/(a+y)<=0. Equality requires y=3a,4a=D^2 and the symmetric endpoint law. For that law F(u)-F(0)=-u^4/[4a(16a^2+4au^2+u^4)]<0 away from zero, so equality is a strict maximum and cannot be a local minimum.
assumptions: mu is a compactly supported probability law

entries.title: P0174 candidate constant one with endpoint check
entries.statement: AUTHOR-CHECKED FULL CANDIDATE, not an independently audited solution: for compactly supported initial probability laws with support diameter D>0, the strict Cauchy-profile minimum bound rules out more than two roots at every level 1/t<=1/D^2. The sufficient Hasebe-Ueda Lemma 3.1 was checked in the cached primary text with semicircle variance t and yields the candidate conclusion of unimodality for t>=D^2. A point mass handles D=0. The symmetric endpoint law fails just below D^2, giving candidate sharp constant C=1. Independent blind KEEP, full proof check, and literature novelty remain outstanding.
assumptions: Cached Lemma 3.1 is used only in its sufficient direction

entries.title: Fixed-mass complement variance identity
entries.statement: For binary occupations on N sites with deterministic total k, S_B=k-S_(B-complement), so Var(S_B)=Var(S_(B-complement))<=min(|B|,N-|B|)^2/4. For a translation-invariant law and a one-site complement, the variance is (k/N)(1-k/N).
entries.proof_text: The complement identity holds for every configuration. A sum over m binary sites has range in [0,m], giving variance at most m^2/4; apply to each complement. Under translation invariance the omitted occupation is Bernoulli with mean k/N.
assumptions: Translation invariance only for the final equality

entries.title: Fixed mass permits ordinary mesoscopic variance
entries.statement: Under the uniform k-subset law on N>=2 sites, a window of m sites has variance m*rho*(1-rho)*(N-m)/(N-1), where rho=k/N. If rho tends to rho_0 in (0,1), m tends to infinity and m/N tends to zero, its variance divided by m tends to rho_0(1-rho_0)>0. This comparison measure is not identified with the ARW free-chain law.
entries.proof_text: Each occupation has mean rho and variance rho(1-rho). Two distinct sites are both occupied with probability k(k-1)/(N(N-1)), giving covariance -rho(1-rho)/(N-1). Summing m variances and m(m-1) covariances gives the formula and its stated limit.

entries.title: Zero-intensity vacant-set walk boundary case
entries.statement: At interlacement intensity u=0 the vacant set is Z^d. For d>=1, simple random walk on it has n^(-1/2) X_(floor(nt)) converging to Brownian motion with covariance t I_d/d. This zero-intensity boundary case does not establish the quenched theorem at positive u.
entries.proof_text: The increments are independent, uniformly distributed on the 2d signed coordinate vectors. Their mean is zero and covariance is I_d/d. The i.i.d.-increment functional central limit theorem gives the claimed covariance and path limit; the environment at u=0 is deterministic.
assumptions: The standard functional CLT for i.i.d. increments

entries.title: Common-time and independent finite-bridge Brownian splices
entries.statement: If for a possibly random T the two path processes X(T+t)-X(T) and X(T-t)-X(T), t>=0, are independent standard Brownian motions, the centered shifted path is standard two-sided Brownian motion. A deterministic finite Brownian bridge segment independent of the two Brownian tails also gives a two-sided Brownian path when concatenated continuously.
entries.proof_text: For the common splice define Y(s)=B-plus(s) for s>=0 and Y(s)=B-minus(-s) for s<=0. Split any family of disjoint increments at zero. Each increment is a sum of independent centered Gaussian Brownian increments, with variance the original interval length, and disjoint increments remain independent. The same splitting at both 0 and a deterministic L proves the three-piece version Y(s)=B-mid(s) on [0,L] and Y(s)=B-mid(L)+B-plus(s-L) above L. Continuity and the Gaussian increment laws identify the two-sided Brownian law.
assumptions: Both entire half-paths have Brownian marginal laws at the proposed splice
The bridge length, if used, is deterministic

entries.title: A future-selected splice can lose Brownian marginals
entries.statement: Let B be standard Brownian motion. Define T=0 when B(1)>0 and T=1 otherwise. Then E[B(T+1)-B(T)]=1/sqrt(2*pi)>0, so the selected one-step increment is not a standard Brownian increment. This T is not assumed to be a stopping time.
entries.proof_text: The expectation is E[B(1) 1_(B(1)>0)] + E[(B(2)-B(1)) 1_(B(1)<=0)]. The second term is zero by independent centered increments. The first is integral_0^infinity z exp(-z^2/2)/sqrt(2*pi) dz=1/sqrt(2*pi).
assumptions: T uses the stated future-dependent selection rule

entries.title: Conditional safe-margin tail and inverse moments
entries.statement: Let K be a deterministic nonempty compact set and F a random closed set in Euclidean space. Suppose for 0<delta<=delta_0 that K has a delta-net with at most C delta^(-d_0) centers in K, and sup_(x in K) P(dist(x,F)<=2delta)<=C-prime delta^alpha with alpha>d_0. For R=dist(K,F), gamma=alpha-d_0 and A=C*C-prime, P(R<=delta)<=A delta^gamma and R>0 almost surely. For 0<p<gamma, E[R^(-p)]<=delta_0^(-p)+A*p*delta_0^(gamma-p)/(gamma-p), taking infinity^(-p)=0.
entries.proof_text: If R<=delta, a closest point of K is within delta of F. A delta-net center is within 2delta of F, so a union bound proves the tail inequality. Letting delta decrease to zero excludes R=0. Compactness of K and closedness of F make disjointness equivalent to positive separation. Apply the layer-cake identity p integral_0^infinity delta^(-p-1)P(R<delta) ddelta, using the tail bound below delta_0 and probability at most one above it. Both integrals give the stated bound. The comparison tail delta^gamma on (0,1) has divergent gamma-th inverse moment, so the endpoint is not guaranteed.

entries.title: Exact DGFF scaling under constant conductance multiplication
entries.statement: On a finite conductance network with Dirichlet boundary and positive-definite unnormalized Dirichlet Laplacian L, a DGFF has covariance L^(-1). Multiplying all conductances by a>0 divides the covariance by a and gives the field law h/sqrt(a).
entries.proof_text: The conductance energy and its Laplacian both multiply by a. The inverse becomes L^(-1)/a. Centered Gaussian laws are determined by their covariances, which equals the covariance of h/sqrt(a).
assumptions: Every interior component reaches the Dirichlet boundary

entries.title: Uniform-ellipticity comparison of DGFF covariance forms
entries.statement: For a finite network as above with lambda<=c_e<=Lambda, 0<lambda<=Lambda, and unit-conductance Dirichlet Laplacian L_0, its DGFF covariance G_c obeys G_0/Lambda<=G_c<=G_0/lambda in quadratic-form order. This controls linear-functional variances and by itself asserts no universal extremal-process law.
entries.proof_text: The edge-energy representation gives lambda L_0<=L_c<=Lambda L_0. For any positive-definite L, f^T L^(-1)f=sup_v(2f^Tv-v^TLv). Increasing L decreases this supremum, so inversion reverses quadratic-form order and proves the sandwich.

entries.title: A qualitative scale limit does not supply bounded cumulative error
entries.statement: The stored C0010 route has not verified a theorem giving the uniform O(1) Green-function remainder needed by its multiscale argument under arbitrary stationary ergodic conductances. Errors e_j=1/j tend to zero while their accumulated sum diverges, so a qualitative limiting estimate alone is insufficient. This is a gap in that route, not a counterexample to the random-conductance DGFF theorem.
assumptions: This warning concerns the cited route, not impossibility of another proof

entries.title: Correct torus crossover comparison and explicit gap sequence
entries.statement: For d>6 and V tending to infinity, V^(-1/3)<<V^(-2/d). With beta=(1/3+2/d)/2 and eps=V^(-beta), eps/V^(-1/3) tends to infinity but eps/V^(-2/d) tends to zero. Thus the entire window-above regime is not above the V^(-2/d) crossover; the stored opposite implication is false.
entries.proof_text: Since 2/d<1/3, V^(-2/d)/V^(-1/3)=V^(1/3-2/d) tends to infinity. The midpoint exponent satisfies 2/d<beta<1/3, so the two eps ratios have respectively positive and negative exponents. Under xi~eps^(-1/2), xi/V^(1/d)=V^(beta/2-1/d) grows along this sequence; that heuristic cannot supply the earlier crossover justification.
assumptions: The symbol << means the ratio tends to zero

entries.title: Integer binomial quadratics have exact trace Laplacian
entries.statement: For every symmetric integer matrix A in dimension d, g_A(x)=sum_i A_ii*x_i*(x_i-1)/2+sum_(i<j) A_ij*x_i*x_j is integer valued on Z^d, differs from x^T A x/2 by a linear term, and has unnormalized nearest-neighbor Laplacian Delta g_A=tr(A). It is a witness for a threshold Delta g<=K when tr(A)<=K, after matching the intended growth convention; no general maximality claim is made.
entries.proof_text: Every x_i(x_i-1) is even. The diagonal binomial term has second difference A_ii in direction i, and each cross term is affine in each coordinate and has zero second difference. Sum over directions to obtain tr(A). Expanding the binomial diagonal terms gives the specified quadratic plus linear term.
assumptions: A is a symmetric integer matrix
K is an explicitly stated threshold

entries.title: Counterexample to the stored ceiling-curvature bound
entries.statement: For g(x)=ceil(a*x^2/2) on Z, the stored bound Delta g<=a+1 is false: a=1/2 gives Delta g(0)=2>3/2. The universally valid rounding estimate is Delta g(x)<a+2 for every real a and integer x.
entries.proof_text: At a=1/2 the values at -1,0,1 are 1,0,1. In general write g(x)=a*x^2/2+e(x) with 0<=e(x)<1. Then Delta g=a+e(x+1)+e(x-1)-2e(x)<a+2.
assumptions: a is real and x is integer

entries.title: Exact finite-quotient approximations for residually finite groups
entries.statement: Every Cayley graph of a finitely generated residually finite group with a finite symmetric generating set is a local weak limit of finite quotient Cayley graphs, with generator labels preserved. For a prescribed radius R, choose a finite-index normal subgroup containing no nonidentity word of length at most 2R+1; every quotient root then has the exact radius-R labelled ball.
entries.proof_text: Residual finiteness separates each of the finitely many nonidentity elements in the word ball of radius 2R+1 in a finite quotient. Intersect these kernels. A collision between two radius-R words would give a kernel word of length <=2R, and an extra edge between them would give one of length <=2R+1; both are excluded. Quotient transitivity makes every root exact. Letting R grow proves uniform-rooted local weak convergence. The labels are inherited from the quotient, so this is the labelled sofic special case.
assumptions: G is finitely generated and residually finite
S is a finite symmetric generating set

entries.title: The finite-quotient case does not resolve unlabelled label recovery
entries.statement: C0148 in the cached Pete notes asks about unlabelled local weak approximations. The residually finite construction supplies labels from actual finite quotients; it does not show that arbitrary unlabelled approximating graphs admit globally compatible generator labels on almost every root. The earlier locally rigid picture has no inspected theorem establishing that compatibility for general groups.
assumptions: The general question concerns unlabelled graphs

entries.title: Self-similar Jordan arcs can force every subarc to have full dimension
entries.statement: Let f:[0,1]->K be a homeomorphism onto a Jordan arc. Suppose for every n and 0<=j<4^n the subarc f([j/4^n,(j+1)/4^n]) is a similarity copy of K, and dim_H K=q. Then every nontrivial Jordan arc A contained in K has Hausdorff dimension q.
entries.proof_text: The compact connected nontrivial set f^(-1)(A) is a nondegenerate closed interval [a,b]. Some base-four subdivision interval is contained in [a,b]. Its image is a similarity copy of K and hence has dimension q. It lies in A, while A lies in K; monotonicity of Hausdorff dimension gives q<=dim_H A<=q.
assumptions: f is a homeomorphism onto a Jordan arc
All canonical base-four subarcs are similarity copies of K

entries.title: Polygonal approximation does not construct thin arcs inside a trace
entries.statement: A continuous planar path and its one-dimensional polygonal approximations do not by themselves produce a one-dimensional Jordan arc contained in the path image. For the standard Koch arc, the similarity dimension is log(4)/log(3)>1 and every nontrivial internal Jordan arc has that dimension. This deterministic obstruction refutes the generic polygonal-approximation route; it asserts no dimension above one for a Brownian trace.
assumptions: The standard Koch arc satisfies the stated self-similar Jordan-arc hypotheses
The usual open-set self-similar dimension theorem is an input
